chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

One of our companions asked him (while I was present) about the Qunut in Friday prayer, so he said to him, 'In the second rak'ah.' He said to him, 'Some of our companions have narrated to us that you said to him, 'In the first rak'ah.' So he said, 'In the last (one).' When he saw confusion in him, he said, 'O Abu Muhammad, in the first and the last.' Abu Basir then asked, 'Before the ruku' or after it?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Every Qunut is before the ruku', except for Friday prayer, for indeed the first rak'ah in it is before the ruku' and the last one is after the ruku'.'
ai.seo_question: When should the Qunut be recited in Friday prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* establishes the specific jurisprudential ruling for Friday prayer, distinguishing it from the general Sunnah of performing Qunut before Ruku'. It highlights the Imam’s patience in clarifying the dual timing—before Ruku' in the first rak'ah and after Ruku' in the second—demonstrating the precision required in ritual worship according to Shia fiqh. This exception underscores the unique status of Jumu'ah as a weekly congregational prayer with distinct liturgical elements.
